A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoC research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original QA experiments on CRUD, DuReader, and WebCPM, alongside chunking-metric evaluations, sensitivity analyses, and training curves.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds timing measurements, attention analyses, repeated-run uncertainty reporting, and correlation estimates.

M1.justification: The GPT-4o data-generation prompt changes its required output from newline/dash-separated chunks in v1 Table 6 to <chunk>...</chunk> wrappers in v2 Table 10. This is a limited output-format revision; the MoC router, experts, training objectives, regex extraction, and edit-distance recovery remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Reported training and benchmark coverage remain the 20,000-example training set and CRUD single-hop/two-hop, DuReader, and WebCPM evaluations. Appendix A.3 announces a 120,000-entry Chinese/English dataset release, but does not establish its use in the reported experiments or an added multilingual evaluation.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same baseline methods. The new timing analysis uses already evaluated methods; the dissimilarity models tabulated in v2 Table 4 already appear in v1 Figure 4, retained as v2 Figure 7.

E3.justification: V2 Appendix A.5 introduces a timing protocol measuring average seconds per CRUD document on one NVIDIA A800 GPU. Existing QA metrics, retrieval settings, average chunk-length control, model configurations, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendices A.5–A.7 substantially expand supporting analyses: runtime comparisons, attention heatmaps before and after fine-tuning, GPT-4o chunk-length variation, and Pearson correlations between chunking metrics and QA performance. Existing placeholder and hyperparameter sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V1 provides point estimates without reported repeated-run uncertainty. V2 Appendix A.6 and Table 8 first report three independent experiments per method and confidence-interval offsets across the main results. The confidence level and interval construction are unspecified; this establishes new reporting, not a demonstrated increase over v1's run count.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and sensitivity scores are unchanged, but substantial supporting results are added. Table 7 reports 1.16, 3.23, 26.99, and 3.69 seconds per document for Semantic Chunking, LumberChunker, Qwen2.5-14B, and Meta-chunker-1.5B. Appendix A.7 reports correlations of 0.8776, -0.7453, and -0.6663; new figures report attention changes and chunk-length variation.

T1.justification: The metric definitions, routing objective, extraction formulation, edit-distance recurrence, and conditional-probability formulation are retained. Changing the node-degree symbol from di to hi is equivalent notation. The added methodological discussion and Pearson analysis introduce no new formal theory or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: direct chunking-quality metrics, limitations of semantic chunking, and efficient granularity-aware MoC using lightweight experts and regex extraction. Added analyses support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: V2 interprets fine-tuning as redirecting attention toward chunk boundaries, discusses sentence-first chunking failures on colloquial and structured text, and explains why reusable knowledge bases can justify chunking overhead. The original dataset-size and multilingual-validation limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 newly reports an open-source 120,000-entry dataset, split equally between Chinese and English, and explains approximately 5,000 examples per granularity label in the original training set. V2 also documents timing hardware and revises the teacher prompt. The explicit Float32 qualifier is removed, while full precision remains stated; code access and training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: The reference list is unchanged. Section 2 adds positioning around API costs and open-model specialization, while Appendix A.6 further distinguishes MoC's direct chunking approach from sentence-segmentation-first methods and their structural limitations.

P1.justification: V2 adds a methodology overview, expands explanatory appendix prose, and inserts three appendix sections before the retained prompt and training sections. Most existing prose remains unchanged; limited edits remove the duplicated introduction question and correct the sensitivity-analysis figure reference.

P2.justification: V2 adds attention heatmaps, a chunk-length plot, and timing, uncertainty, and correlation tables. Table 4 additionally tabulates part of the existing metric comparison. Original figures are retained under matched numbering, while tables move and the two prompt displays are reformatted together on the final page.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens v1's supporting evidence through measured runtime, explicit metric correlations, repeated-run reporting, and expanded data documentation. These gains are limited: confidence-interval construction is unspecified, correlations use only four methods, and timing measures Meta-chunker rather than the full MoC pipeline. The additions improve scrutiny and transparency without substantially resolving these validation gaps.
